title: Embedding Workload Canary and Capacity Runbook
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Overview

Purpose: This runbook defines the canary and capacity-management procedures for embedding-generation workloads (batch and low-latency single-call paths). It is intended for SREs, model-serving owners, and platform engineers running Redwood Dedicated or Private deployments where embedding traffic can materially affect GPU memory and inference throughput.

Scope: applies to: embedding endpoints (v1/embeddings, v2/embeddings), dedicated GPU pools used for embedding models, and shared pools with mixed generation & embedding traffic. Excludes offline large-batch training jobs.

Key goals
- Protect SLOs for embedding latency and success rate during rollouts.
- Provide deterministic capacity checks and preflight validations for embedding model variants and quantization profiles.
- Safe canary release and rollback steps with observability and automated thresholds.

Service-level objectives (SLOs) & error budget model
- Primary SLO: 99.9% of embedding requests (per-minute windows) must complete successfully (HTTP 2xx) and with p99 latency <= 150ms for single-vector generation on production instance types (A10G / H100 equivalents).
- Secondary SLO: Throughput SLO for batch embedding pipelines: sustained throughput within 10% of target configured QPS for the pool across 95% of 1-hour windows.
- Error budget: Defined per-service and per-tenant. 30-day window; alert at 25% consumption, paging at 50%. Error budget consumption due to capacity (OOS/evictions) is counted separately and triggers capacity reviews.

Capacity planning checklist (pre-canary)
1) Model footprint and peak memory
- Document model size (FP16/4-bit quantized) and expected KV cache usage for the longest sequence length. Example table: 
| Model | Params | Quantized size | Expected cache (MB) | Memory headroom per GPU |
| embed-2-small | 2B | 4.8 GB (4-bit) | 128 MB | 12 GB |
| embed-10-large | 10B | 22 GB (FP16) | 512 MB | 6 GB |

2) Pool sizing heuristic
- Preferred: maintain >= 20% free GPU memory headroom on each node for embedding bursts.
- Throughput estimate: QPS_per_gpu = floor((GPU_memory - model_memory - cache_margin) / per_request_memory) * batching_efficiency_factor.
- Use the provided capacity check script (example below) to compute expected QPS before canary.

3) Capacity safety nets
- Reserve a small pool of prewarmed nodes (min_reserve: 2 nodes or 10% of pool, whichever is larger) to absorb sudden increases in embedding traffic.
- Autoscale policy: scale_up_delta = +2 nodes on 5-minute sustained CPU/GPU util > 75% and p95_latency degradation > 30%.

Preflight validations (automated)
- Smoke tests: run reference embedding suite (10 queries, varied dimensions and sequence lengths) against canary instances. All must return valid vectors (no NaNs) and pass cosine-stability check (cosine similarity to baseline > 0.995).
- Perf regression test: run p95/p99 microbench for single-call latency and batch path. Regression threshold: no more than +10% relative increase in p95 and +5% in p99 versus baseline variant.
- Resource audit: check kernel selection and memory planner logs for unexpected allocations.

Canary rollout procedure (stable -> canary -> ramp)
1) Create canary version: push model variant and runtime config to the staging pool. Tag: canary/<model>/<sha>-<date>.
2) Run preflight smoke and perf validations. Block if any check fails.
3) Canary traffic allocation: start at 1% traffic for 15 minutes, then evaluate metrics. If stable, 5% for 30 minutes, then 15% for 60 minutes, then 50% for 60 minutes, then 100% cutover. Each step requires explicit pass of verification checks.
4) Verification checks (per step):
- Success rate >= 99.95% for the canary cohort.
- p99 latency for canary cohort <= SLO_threshold * 1.05.
- Error budget burn for main production cohort does not accelerate by >10% vs baseline trend.
- No increase in OOM/eviction events per node (zero tolerated in first two steps).

5) Automated rollback triggers (immediate):
- Canaries returning >0.5% 5xx errors in a 5m window.
- p99 degradation > 25% vs baseline for the canary cohort.
- Node-level GPU memory OOM or eviction detected.
- Autoscale fails to add nodes within configured window and p95 latency remains >150ms for 10 minutes.

Manual rollback criteria (escalation to oncall):
- Subtle quality regressions surfaced by evals tied to real prompts (semantic drift).
- Error budget consumption accelerating beyond 50% within 24 hours of rollout.

Runbook steps for an automated rollback (immediate action)
1) Abort traffic ramp: set traffic split to 0% for canary cohort via routing API:
curl -X POST https://console.redwood.internal/api/v1/routing/split \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"model":"embed-10-large","canary":0}'
2) De-orphan canary hosts: mark nodes as drain=false, restart serving process if necessary:
kubectl annotate nodes <node> redwood/drain=false && kubectl rollout restart deployment/embed-serving --namespace=redwood-serving
3) Capture forensic evidence: collect heap profiles, nvml logs, kernel traces, and the canary request IDs (export using /internal/trace/export). Save to /var/rt/forensics/<incident-id>.tar.gz.
4) Notify stakeholders: Page oncall, notify product owner, and open an incident review ticket with initial findings.

Observability and telemetry requirements
- Dashboards (must exist and be checked at each canary step):
  - Canary cohort health: success-rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, request-per-second, average tokens-per-request.
  - Node health: GPU memory used, GPU util, out_of_memory_count, process_restarts, scheduler_queue_length.
  - Model-level cost indicators: tokens-per-second and estimated $/hour for active nodes.
- Alerts and thresholds:
  - Page: error_rate > 0.5% in 5m, p99 latency > 250ms sustained 10m, GPU OOM event count >= 1 in 5m.
  - Warning: p95 increased by 20% in 10m, node GPU util > 90% for 15m.

Incident review standards (what to collect and how to write the review)
- Minimum evidence set: timeline (UTC), service and node metrics, orchestration events (scale up/down), config diffs (model weights/quantization flags), request samples, and golden prompt regressions.
- Attach forensic artifacts: nvml logs, core dumps (if available), GC/heap snapshots, and relevant git SHAs.
- Root cause guidance: document O(1) causes (OOM, new kernel regressions, batching behavior changes, packing algorithm regressions, aggressive quantization).
- Outcome classification: revert, patch, config-tweak, capacity-increase, or follow-up engineering task.
- Postmortem timeline: initial incident ticket within 1 hour, bridge summary within 3 hours, blameless postmortem draft within 72 hours, final review in the fortnight retro.

Operational tooling & scripts (examples)
- capacity-check.sh (pseudo snippet):
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# usage: ./capacity-check.sh <model-quantized-size-GB> <gpu-memory-GB>
model_size=$1
gpu_mem=$2
headroom=$(python - <<PY
print(max(0, $gpu_mem - $model_size - 2))
PY)
echo "Estimated memory headroom: ${headroom}GB"

- ramp-traffic.py (example):
# ramp traffic via routing API with wait and verification hooks (pseudo)
- verify-smoke.py: run embedding stability checks and cosine similarity assertions.

Reliability initiatives and drills (recommended cadence)
- Monthly miniature canary drills: pick a low-traffic model variant and practice a full 1%->100% ramp in a sandbox region. Record time to detect failures and time to rollback.
- Quarterly stress tests: synthetic workloads that push batch embedding throughput to 120% of expected peak across 6-hour windows.
- Annual cost-and-capacity audit: validate pool sizing heuristics against actual 12-month traffic patterns and update safety margins.

Appendix: sample verification checklist (copyable)
- [ ] smoke tests passed (10/10)
- [ ] perf regressions within thresholds (p95 <= +10%, p99 <= +5%)
- [ ] memory headroom >= 20% per node
- [ ] reserve nodes healthy and in Ready state
- [ ] dashboards populated with real-time cohort split
- [ ] automated rollback hooks configured and tested
